opening_story.en:
Meet Emeka.

Emeka is 24, from Onitsha. He grew up hearing the same things every Nigerian boy hears:

"Real men don't cry." "You are the man — you must provide." "Control your woman or she will disrespect you."

His father said it. His uncles said it. His church said it. His friends still say it.

But lately, Emeka has been thinking. His younger sister was beaten by her boyfriend. When Emeka told his uncle, the uncle said — "Maybe she provoked him. A man has to show authority."

Emeka felt something wrong with that answer. But he didn't have the words to explain why.

Today, we give him — and you — those words.
opening_story.pcm:
Meet Emeka.

Emeka dey 24, from Onitsha. E grow up dey hear wetin every Nigerian boy dey hear:

"Real men no dey cry." "You be the man — you gatz provide." "Control your woman or she go disrespect you."

Im papa talk am. Im uncles talk am. Im church talk am. Im friends still dey talk am.

But lately, Emeka don dey think. Im younger sister don collect beating from her boyfriend. When Emeka tell im uncle, the uncle talk — "Maybe she provoke am. Man gatz show authority."

Emeka feel say something no dey right with that answer. But e no get the words to explain why.

Today, we go give am — and you — those words.
opening_story.ha:
Gane Emeka.

Emeka yana da shekaru 24, daga Onitsha. Ya tashi yana jin abubuwan da kowanne yaro na Najeriya ke ji:

"Maza na gaskiya ba sa kuka." "Kai ne namijin — dole ne ka samar." "Ka kula da matarka ko zata yi maka rashin girmamawa."

Ubangijinsa ya fada. 'Yan uwansa sun fada. Coci ya fada. Abokansa har yanzu suna fada.

Amma a yanzu, Emeka yana tunani. Kanwar sa ta karbi dukan daga namijin da take soyayya da shi. Lokacin da Emeka ya gaya wa 'yan uwansa, 'yan uwansa sun ce — "Wata kila ta tayar da shi. Namijin yana da hakkin nuna iko."

Emeka ya ji cewa akwai wani abu da ba daidai ba a wannan amsar. Amma ba shi da kalmomi don bayyana dalilin.

A yau, za mu ba shi — da ku — wadannan kalmomi.
opening_story.yo:
Pẹ̀lú Emeka.

Emeka jẹ́ ọmọ ọdún 24, láti Onitsha. Ó dàgbà tí ó ń gbọ́ ohun tí gbogbo ọmọkùnrin Nàìjíríà ń gbọ́:

"Àwọn ọkùnrin gidi kò ní sunkún." "Ìwọ ni ọkùnrin — o gbọdọ̀ pèsè." "Ṣàkóso obìnrin rẹ, tàbí yóò bínú sí ẹ." 

Baba rẹ sọ̀rọ̀ yìí. Àwọn ìyá rẹ sọ̀rọ̀ yìí. Ìjọ wọn sọ̀rọ̀ yìí. Àwọn ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ ṣi ń sọ̀rọ̀ yìí.

Ṣùgbọ́n laipẹ, Emeka ti ń rò. Àbúrò rẹ ti gba ìyà láti ọkùnrin tó ń bá a. Nígbà tí Emeka sọ fún ìyá rẹ, ìyá rẹ sọ pé — "Bóyá ó ti fa a. Ọkùnrin gbọdọ̀ fi àṣẹ hàn."

Emeka ní ìmọ̀ràn pé ohun kan kò tọ́ ní ìdáhùn yẹn. Ṣùgbọ́n kò ní àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ láti ṣàlàyé ìdí.

Lónìí, a máa fún un — àti ẹ — ní àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ wọ̀nyí.
opening_story.ig:
Nabata Emeka.

Emeka bụ afọ 24, si Onitsha. Ọ tozuru oke na-anụ otu ihe niile nwa nwoke Nigeria na-anụ:

"Ndị nwoke ziri ezi anaghị egbu egbu." "Ị bụ nwoke — ị ga-enyere." "Jide nwanyị gị ma ọ bụ ọ ga-eme gị ihe na-adịghị mma."

Nna ya kwuru ya. Ụmụnna ya kwuru ya. Ụka ha kwuru ya. Ndị enyi ya ka na-ekwu ya.

Ma n'oge a, Emeka na-eche. Nwanne ya nwanyị natara ịkụda site n'aka nwoke ya. Mgbe Emeka gwara Ụmụnna ya, Ụmụnna ya kwuru — "O nwere ike na ọ kpaliri ya. Nwoke ga-egosi ọchịchị."

Emeka chọpụtara na ihe dị na azịza ahụ. Ma ọ nweghị okwu iji kọwaa ihe kpatara ya.

Taa, anyị ga-enye ya — na gị — okwu ndị ahụ.

content.en:
These two words are often used as if they mean the same thing. They do not.

SEX is biological — the body you were born with. Male or female. Determined by chromosomes, hormones, and anatomy.

GENDER is social — the rules, roles, and expectations that society places on people because of their sex.

One comes from nature. The other was built by people.
content.pcm:
Dis two words dey often use like say dem mean the same thing. Dem no mean the same.

SEX na biological — di body wey you born with. Male or female. Na chromosomes, hormones, and anatomy dey determine am.

GENDER na social — di rules, roles, and expectations wey society dey put for people because of dem sex.

One come from nature. Di other one na people build am.
content.ha:
Wannan kalmomi biyu ana yawan amfani da su kamar suna nufin abu daya. Ba su nufin abu daya ba.

JINS na jiki — jikin da aka haife ka da shi. Namijin ko mace. Ana tantance shi ta hanyar chromosomes, hormones, da anatomy.

JINS na zamantakewa — dokoki, rawar da ake takawa, da tsammanin da al'umma ke sanya wa mutane saboda jinsinsu.

Daya yana fitowa daga halitta. Wani an gina shi ta hanyar mutane.
content.yo:
Àwọn ọ̀rọ̀ méjèèjì yìí ni a máa ń lò gẹ́gẹ́ bíi pé wọ́n túmọ̀ sí ohun kan. Wọ́n kò túmọ̀ sí ohun kan.

ÌBÁṢEPO jẹ́ ti ẹ̀dá — ara tí a bí ẹ̀. Ọkùnrin tàbí obìnrin. A ṣe àfihàn rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú chromosomes, hormones, àti anatomy.

JINSI jẹ́ ti awujọ — àwọn òfin, ipa, àti ìretí tí awujọ fi ń lé àwọn ènìyàn lórí nítorí ìbáṣepọ wọn.

Ọkan wá láti inú ẹ̀dá. Ẹlòmíràn ni àwọn ènìyàn kọ́.
content.ig:
A na-ejikarị okwu abụọ a eme ihe dịka ha pụtara otu ihe. Ha adịghị.

Ndị nwoke bụ nke anụ ahụ — ahụ ị mụrụ na ya. Nwoke ma ọ bụ nwanyị. A na-achọpụta ya site na chromosomes, hormones, na anatomy.

Ụmụ nwanyị bụ nke mmekọrịta — iwu, ọrụ, na atụmanya nke ọha na eze na-etinye na ndị mmadụ n'ihi ụdị ha.

Otu na-abịa site na okike. Nke ọzọ bụ ndị mmadụ wulite.

content.en:
Here is the most important thing we will say in this entire course:

You were born male. But everything you learned about "how to be a man" — that was taught to you.

By your father. Your uncles. Your school. Your religion. Your community. Your peers.

Some of those lessons were good and worth keeping. Some were harmful — and can be changed.
content.pcm:
Here na di most important thing we go talk for dis entire course:

You born male. But everything wey you learn about "how to be a man" — dem teach you.

By your papa. Your uncles. Your school. Your religion. Your community. Your peers.

Some of those lessons dey good and worth keeping. Some dey harmful — and fit change.
content.ha:
Ga abin da ya fi muhimmanci da za mu fada a cikin wannan dukan kwas:

An haife ka namijin. Amma duk abin da ka koya game da "yadda za a zama namijin" — an koya maka.

Ta hanyar ubanka. 'Yan uwanka. Makarantarka. Addininka. Al'ummarka. Abokan aikinka.

Wasu daga cikin wadannan darussan suna da kyau kuma suna da amfani. Wasu suna da lahani — kuma za a iya canza su.
content.yo:
Eyi ni ohun tó ṣe pàtàkì jùlọ tí a ó sọ nínú gbogbo ẹ̀kọ́ yìí:

A bí ẹ́ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ọkùnrin. Ṣùgbọ́n gbogbo ohun tí o kọ́ nípa "báwo ni a ṣe lè jẹ́ ọkùnrin" — a kọ́ ọ.

Nípasẹ̀ baba rẹ. Àwọn ìyá rẹ. Ilé ẹ̀kọ́ rẹ. Ẹ̀sìn rẹ. Àwùjọ rẹ. Àwọn ẹlẹ́gbẹ́ rẹ.

Diẹ̀ lára àwọn ẹ̀kọ́ wọ̀nyí dára àti pé ó yẹ kí o pa wọn mọ́. Diẹ̀ sì jẹ́ ìfarapa — àti pé a lè yí wọn padà.
content.ig:
Nke a bụ ihe kachasị mkpa anyị ga-ekwu na nke a niile:

A mụrụ gị dịka nwoke. Ma ihe niile ị mụtara banyere "otu esi abụ nwoke" — a kụziri gị.

Site n'aka nna gị. Ụmụnna gị. Ụlọ akwụkwọ gị. Okpukpe gị. Ọha gị. Ndị ikwu gị.

Ụfọdụ n’ime ọmụmụ ndị ahụ bụ ezigbo ihe ma kwesịrị ka e chekwaa. Ụfọdụ nwere ihe ọjọọ — ma enwere ike ịgbanwe ha.

title.ig: Kedu ihe bụ Ụmụ nwoke Ziri Ezi?

content.en:
Masculinity is the way men express themselves in the world. But there is not just one way to be a man.

Harmful masculinity says: dominate, control, never feel.

Positive masculinity says: lead with respect, feel without shame, protect without controlling, be strong AND kind.

One traps you. The other sets you free. This course is about choosing freedom.
content.pcm:
Masculinity na di way men dey express demself for di world. But no be only one way to be man.

Harmful masculinity dey talk: dominate, control, no dey feel.

Positive masculinity dey talk: lead with respect, feel without shame, protect without controlling, be strong AND kind.

One dey trap you. Di other one dey set you free. Dis course na about choosing freedom.
content.ha:
Namijin yana nufin yadda maza ke bayyana kansu a duniya. Amma ba hanya guda daya ce ta zama namijin ba.

Namijin da ke cutarwa yana cewa: yi iko, kula, kada ka ji.

Kyakkyawan namijin yana cewa: jagoranci tare da girmamawa, ji ba tare da kunya ba, kare ba tare da iko ba, zama mai karfi DA kirki.

Daya yana kulle ka. Wani yana saki ka. Wannan kwas yana magana ne akan zabar 'yanci.'
content.yo:
Ìbáṣepọ jẹ́ bí àwọn ọkùnrin ṣe ń fi ara wọn hàn nínú ayé. Ṣùgbọ́n kò sí ọ̀nà kan ṣoṣo láti jẹ́ ọkùnrin.

Ìbáṣepọ tó ń fa ìfarapa sọ pé: jẹ́ aláṣẹ, ṣàkóso, má ṣe ní ìmọ̀lára.

Ìbáṣepọ tó dára sọ pé: jẹ́ olórí pẹ̀lú ìbáṣepọ, ní ìmọ̀lára láì ní ìkà, dáàbò bo láì ṣàkóso, jẹ́ alágbára ÀTI aláàánú.

Ọkan ń pa ẹ́. Ẹlòmíràn ń tú ẹ́ sílẹ̀. Ẹ̀kọ́ yìí jẹ́ nípa yíyan ìyàtọ̀.
content.ig:
Ụmụ nwoke bụ ụzọ ndị nwoke si egosi onwe ha na ụwa. Ma ọ bụghị naanị otu ụzọ ka e si abụ nwoke.

Ụmụ nwoke na-emebi emebi na-ekwu: jide, jide, echefu.

Ụmụ nwoke ziri ezi na-ekwu: duzie na nsọpụrụ, nwee mmetụta na-enweghị ihere, chebe na-enweghị ijide, bụrụ ike NA obiọma.

Otu na-ejide gị. Nke ọzọ na-eme ka ị nwee nnwere onwe. Nke a bụ banyere ịhọrọ nnwere onwe.

title.ha: Hanyoyin Da Suka Jawo Matsala & Maza Masu Guba

opening_story.en:
Meet Aondo.

Aondo is 19, from Makurdi. When his best friend Osas started crying after losing his job, Aondo felt deeply uncomfortable.

He told Osas: "Oga, men don't cry. Pull yourself together."

Three weeks later, Osas stopped answering his phone. His family found him in his room. He had taken his own life.

Aondo has not forgiven himself since. He keeps asking: "What if I had let him cry? What if I had just listened?"

Today, we explore the norms that told Aondo — and all of us — that men cannot feel. And what those norms cost us.
opening_story.pcm:
Meet Aondo.

Aondo dey 19, from Makurdi. When him best friend Osas start to cry after him lose him job, Aondo feel very uncomfortable.

Him tell Osas: "Oga, men no dey cry. Pull yourself together."

Three weeks later, Osas stop to answer him phone. Him family find am for him room. Him don take him own life.

Aondo never forgive himself since then. Him dey ask: "What if I let am cry? What if I just listen?"

Today, we go explore the norms wey tell Aondo — and all of us — say men no fit feel. And wetin those norms cost us.
opening_story.ha:
Gani Aondo.

Aondo yana da shekara 19, daga Makurdi. Lokacin da abokinsa Osas ya fara kuka bayan ya rasa aikinsa, Aondo ya ji rashin jin daɗi sosai.

Ya gaya wa Osas: "Oga, maza ba sa kuka. Ka daure kanka."

Bayan makonni uku, Osas ya daina amsa wayarsa. Iyalan sa sun same shi a dakin sa. Ya dauki rayuwarsa.

Aondo bai yafe wa kansa tun daga lokacin ba. Yana ci gaba da tambaya: "Me zai faru idan na bari ya kuka? Me zai faru idan na saurari shi?"

A yau, zamu bincika hanyoyin da suka gaya wa Aondo — da dukkanmu — cewa maza ba sa jin zafi. Kuma menene waɗannan hanyoyin suka jawo mana.
opening_story.yo:
E kaaro Aondo.

Aondo ni ọdun 19, lati Makurdi. Nigbati ọrẹ rẹ Osas bẹrẹ si rò lẹ́yìn tí ó padà iṣẹ́ rẹ, Aondo ní ìmọ̀lára àìlera.

Ó sọ fún Osas pé: "Oga, awọn ọkunrin kò ní rò. Dárúkọ ara rẹ."

Ọsẹ mẹta lẹhinna, Osas dá a láti fèsì sí tẹlifóònù rẹ. Ẹbí rẹ rí i ní ilé rẹ. Ó ti gba ìyàwó rẹ.

Aondo kò tii dárúkọ ara rẹ láti ìgbà yẹn. Ó ń béèrè: "Kí ni yóò ṣẹlẹ̀ bí mo bá jẹ́ kí ó rò? Kí ni yóò ṣẹlẹ̀ bí mo bá jẹ́ kí n gbọ́?"

Loni, a máa ṣàwárí àwọn iwa tó sọ fún Aondo — àti gbogbo wa — pé àwọn ọkunrin kò lè ní ìmọ̀lára. Kí ni àwọn iwa wọ̀nyí ti jẹ́ wa.
opening_story.ig:
Ndewo Aondo.

Aondo bụ afọ 19, si Makurdi. Mgbe enyi ya Osas malitere ịkụda mmiri n'anya mgbe o tufuru ọrụ ya, Aondo chọpụtara na ọ na-enwe mmetụta na-adịghị mma.

O gwara Osas: "Oga, ụmụ nwoke anaghị akwụsị. Nwee onwe gị."

Izu atọ ka e mesịrị, Osas kwụsịrị ịza ekwentị ya. Ezinụlọ ya chọpụtara ya n'ụlọ ya. O were ndụ ya.

Aondo adịghị ewere onwe ya n'obi kemgbe ahụ. Ọ na-ajụ: "Gịnị ma ọ bụrụ na m hapụrụ ya ka ọ kụọ? Gịnị ma ọ bụrụ na m nụrụ ya?"

Taa, anyị ga-enyocha iwu ndị gwara Aondo — na anyị niile — na ụmụ nwoke enweghị ike ịnwe mmetụta. Na ihe iwu ndị ahụ na-eri anyị.

title.ha: Menene Hanyoyin Da Suka Jawo Matsala?

content.en:
Harmful gender norms are beliefs about men that sound like truth but are actually damaging.

They include: "A man must never show weakness." "Men are naturally aggressive — it's in their nature." "A real man controls his household." "If a woman disrespects you, you have the right to correct her."

These are not facts. They are teachings. And they cause real damage — to women, children, and men themselves.
content.pcm:
Harmful gender norms na beliefs about men wey fit sound like truth but e dey damage.

Dem include: "A man no suppose show weakness." "Men dey aggressive by nature — na wetin dey their nature." "A real man dey control him household." "If woman disrespect you, you get right to correct am."

These no be facts. Dem na teachings. And dem dey cause real damage — to women, children, and men themselves.
content.ha:
Hanyoyin da suka jawo matsala suna nufin ra'ayoyi game da maza waɗanda suke kamar gaskiya amma suna jawo lahani.

Sun haɗa da: "Namijin ba zai taɓa nuna rauni ba." "Maza suna da ƙarfi a halitta — yana cikin halayensu." "Namijin gaskiya yana sarrafa gidan sa." "Idan mace ta yi maka rashin girmamawa, kana da hakkin gyara ta."

Wannan ba gaskiya bane. Waɗannan koyarwa ne. Kuma suna jawo lahani mai yawa — ga mata, yara, da maza kansu.
content.yo:
Iwa ibi jẹ́ ìmọ̀ràn nípa àwọn ọkunrin tó dájú pé ó dájú ṣùgbọ́n tó n fa ìfarapa.

Wọ́n ní: "Ọkùnrin kò gbọdọ̀ fi àìlera hàn." "Àwọn ọkunrin ni àìlera nípa ìhà — ó wà nínú ìhà wọn." "Ọkùnrin gidi ni yóò ṣàkóso ilé rẹ." "Bí obìnrin bá ṣe ìbànújẹ́ rẹ, o ní ẹ̀tọ́ láti tọ́ka sí i."

Eyi kì í ṣe òtítọ́. Wọ́n jẹ́ ẹ̀kọ́. Àti pé wọ́n fa ìfarapa gidi — sí àwọn obìnrin, àwọn ọmọ, àti àwọn ọkunrin fúnra wọn.
content.ig:
Iwu ọjọọ bụ echiche banyere ụmụ nwoke nke na-adị ka eziokwu ma na-emebi.

Ha gụnyere: "Nwoke ekwesịghị igosi adịghị ike." "Ụmụ nwoke bụ ndị na-eme ihe ike — ọ bụ n'ịhụnanya ha." "Nwoke ziri ezi na-achị ụlọ ya." "Ọ bụrụ na nwanyị na-emeghị gị mma, ị nwere ikike ịtọpụ ya."

Nke a abụghị eziokwu. Ha bụ ọmụmụ. Na ha na-ebute ezigbo mmebi — na ụmụ nwanyị, ụmụaka, na ụmụ nwoke n'onwe ha.

content.en:
Toxic masculinity is not an insult to men. It is the name for a specific set of harmful ideas about manhood.

It describes behaviours and beliefs like: using violence to show strength, suppressing all emotion except anger, believing women must be controlled, seeing asking for help as weakness, and using sexual conquest to prove manhood.

Toxic masculinity hurts the men who practice it — with mental illness, isolation, and broken relationships — and it hurts everyone around them.
content.pcm:
Toxic masculinity no be insult to men. Na the name for specific set of harmful ideas about manhood.

E dey describe behaviours and beliefs like: using violence to show strength, suppressing all emotion except anger, believing say women suppose dey controlled, seeing asking for help as weakness, and using sexual conquest to prove manhood.

Toxic masculinity dey hurt the men wey dey practice am — with mental illness, isolation, and broken relationships — and e dey hurt everybody around dem.
content.ha:
Maza masu guba ba su zama wani zagi ga maza ba. Sunan ne na wani takamaiman tarin ra'ayoyi masu cutarwa game da namijin.

Yana bayyana halaye da ra'ayoyi kamar: amfani da tashin hankali don nuna ƙarfi, ɓoye dukkan jin daɗi sai fushi, yarda cewa mata dole ne a sarrafa su, ganin neman taimako a matsayin rauni, da amfani da cin nasarar jima'i don tabbatar da namijin.

Maza masu guba suna cutar da mazan da ke aikata su — tare da cututtukan tunani, keɓewa, da dangantaka marasa kyau — kuma suna cutar da kowa a kusa da su.
content.yo:
Iwa maza tóxíc kì í ṣe ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn ọkunrin. Ó jẹ́ orúkọ fún àkójọpọ̀ àwọn ìmọ̀ràn tó n fa ìfarapa nípa ìwa ọkùnrin.

Ó n ṣàpèjúwe àwọn ìhà àti ìmọ̀ràn bí: lílo ìkà láti fi hàn ìṣàkóso, pa gbogbo ìmọ̀lára mọ́ àfi ìbànújẹ́, gbagbọ́ pé obìnrin gbọdọ̀ jẹ́ àkóso, rí i pé béèrè fún ìrànlọ́wọ́ jẹ́ àìlera, àti lílo ìkà jìmọ̀ láti fi hàn ìwa ọkùnrin.

Iwa maza tóxíc n fa ìfarapa sí àwọn ọkunrin tó n ṣe é — pẹ̀lú àìlera ọpọlọ, ìkànsí, àti ìbáṣepọ̀ tó rọrùn — àti pé ó n fa ìfarapa sí gbogbo ènìyàn tó wà ní àgbègbè wọn.
content.ig:
Iwu mazi tóxíc abụghị ihe na-emegide ụmụ nwoke. Ọ bụ aha maka setịpụ nke echiche ọjọọ banyere ịbụ nwoke.

Ọ na-akọwa omume na echiche dịka: iji ihe ike gosi ike, igbochi mmetụta niile ma e wezụga iwe, ikwere na ụmụ nwanyị kwesịrị ịchịkwa, ịhụ na ịrịọ maka enyemaka bụ adịghị ike, na iji ịrụ ọrụ mmekọahụ gosi ịbụ nwoke.

Iwu mazi tóxíc na-emebi ụmụ nwoke na-eme ya — na ọrịa uche, ịkpa, na mmekọrịta mebiri emebi — na ọ na-emebi onye ọ bụla nọ gburugburu ha.

content.en:
In Nigeria, men die younger than women. Men are less likely to see a doctor. Men are more likely to take their own lives in silence.

This is not because men are weaker. It is because they are taught that seeking help is shameful.

The same norms that harm women are slowly destroying men from the inside.

Changing these norms is not about making men weak. It is about keeping men alive, healthy, and connected to the people they love.
content.pcm:
For Nigeria, men dey die younger than women. Men dey less likely to see doctor. Men dey more likely to take their own lives in silence.

This no be because men dey weaker. Na because dem dey teach say seeking help na shame.

The same norms wey dey harm women dey slowly dey destroy men from inside.

Changing these norms no be about making men weak. Na about keeping men alive, healthy, and connected to the people wey dem love.
content.ha:
A Najeriya, maza suna mutuwa da wuri fiye da mata. Maza suna da ƙarancin yiwuwar ganin likita. Maza suna da yawan daukar rayuwarsu a cikin shiru.

Wannan ba saboda maza suna rauni ba. Wannan yana faruwa ne saboda ana koya musu cewa neman taimako abin kunya ne.

Hanyoyin da ke cutar da mata suna raguwa suna lalata maza daga ciki.

Canza waɗannan hanyoyin ba yana nufin sanya maza rauni ba. Yana nufin kiyaye maza cikin rai, lafiya, da haɗin kai da mutanen da suke son su.
content.yo:
Ní Nàìjíríà, àwọn ọkunrin n kú pẹ̀lú àkókò kéré ju àwọn obìnrin lọ. Àwọn ọkunrin kì í ṣe àkóso láti rí dókítà. Àwọn ọkunrin n kópa láti gba ìyàwó wọn ní ìkànsí.

Eyi kì í ṣe nítorí pé àwọn ọkunrin n ra ìlera. Ó jẹ́ nítorí pé wọ́n n kọ́ wọn pé ìbéèrè fún ìrànlọ́wọ́ jẹ́ ìbànújẹ́.

Àwọn iwa tó n fa ìfarapa sí àwọn obìnrin n lọ́wọ́ n pa àwọn ọkunrin láti inú.

Yíyí àwọn iwa wọ̀nyí kì í ṣe pé a fẹ́ jẹ́ kí àwọn ọkunrin jẹ́ àìlera. Ó jẹ́ pé a fẹ́ jẹ́ kí àwọn ọkunrin wa, ní ilera, àti ní ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n nífẹ̀ẹ́.
content.ig:
Na Nigeria, ụmụ nwoke na-anwụ ngwa ngwa karịa ụmụ nwanyị. Ụmụ nwoke na-erughị ala ịhụ dọkịta. Ụmụ nwoke na-enwekarị onwe ha n'ịkpa.

Nke a abụghị n'ihi na ụmụ nwoke na-adịghị ike. Ọ bụ n'ihi na a na-akụziri ha na ịchọ enyemaka bụ ihe na-adịghị mma.

Iwu ndị na-emebi ụmụ nwanyị na-emebi ụmụ nwoke n'ime.

Iji gbanwee iwu ndị a abụghị banyere ime ka ụmụ nwoke bụrụ ndị na-adịghị ike. Ọ bụ banyere ịchekwa ụmụ nwoke ka ha dị ndụ, dị mma, na jikọtara na ndị ha hụrụ n'anya.

opening_story.en:
Meet Musa.

Musa is 26, from Kaduna. One evening, his neighbour Fatima knocked on his door with a swollen face and trembling hands. She said her husband had beaten her again.

Musa felt something rise in his chest. But then he heard his father's voice: "Don't enter another man's marriage. It's not your business."

So Musa said: "Sorry, aunty. Go and settle it between yourselves."

Fatima went home. Two months later, she was admitted to hospital.

Today, Musa is a man who wishes he had known better. This module gives you the knowledge Musa needed.

Gane Musa.

Musa yana da shekaru 26, daga Kaduna. Wata rana, makwabcinsa Fatima ta danna ƙofar sa da fuska mai kumburi da hannaye masu rawa. Ta ce mijinta ya sake dukan ta.

Musa ya ji wani abu ya tashi a cikin kirjin sa. Amma daga bisani ya ji muryar mahaifinsa: "Kada ka shiga cikin aure na wani. Ba harkarka ba ne."

Don haka Musa ya ce: "Yi hakuri, aunty. Je ku warware shi tsakanin ku."

Fatima ta tafi gida. Bayan watanni biyu, an shigar da ita asibiti.

A yau, Musa mutum ne wanda yake son ya san mafi kyau. Wannan module yana ba ku ilimin da Musa ya bukata.
opening_story.yo:

Musa ni ọdun 26, lati Kaduna. Ni irọlẹ kan, aladani rẹ Fatima kọ́kọ́ si ilẹ̀ rẹ pẹ̀lú oju ti o ni irẹwẹsi ati ọwọ́ ti n rọ. O sọ pé ọkọ rẹ ti lu u lẹ́ẹ̀kan si i.

Musa ní ìmọ̀ràn kan tó dide nínú ẹ̀jẹ̀ rẹ. Ṣùgbọ́n nígbà náà, ó gbọ́ ohùn baba rẹ: "Má bọ́ sí ìyàwó ẹlòmíràn. Kò jẹ́ ọ́rọ̀ rẹ."

Nítorí náà, Musa sọ pé: "Ẹ jọ̀ọ́, aunty. Ẹ lọ dá a lára yín."

Fatima lọ sí ilé. Oṣù méjì lẹ́yìn náà, wọ́n wọ́ ọ́ sí ilé ìwòsàn.

Loni, Musa jẹ́ ọkùnrin tó fẹ́ kí ó ti mọ̀ pé ó dára jù. Ẹ̀kọ́ yìí máa fún ọ ní ìmọ̀ tó yẹ ki Musa ní.
opening_story.ig:
Nụ Musa.

Musa bụ afọ 26, si Kaduna. Otu mgbede, onye agbata obi ya Fatima kpọrọ ọnụ ụzọ ya nwere ihu na-agbaji na aka na-ama jijiji. O kwuru na di ya akpọrọ ya ọzọ.

Musa chọpụtara ihe na-arịgo n'obi ya. Ma mgbe ahụ, o nụrụ olu nna ya: "Ekwela ka ị banye n'ịlụ di nke ọzọ. Ọ bụghị ọrụ gị."

Ya mere Musa kwuru: "Ndo, aunty. Gaa dozie ya n'etiti unu."

Fatima gara n'ụlọ. Oge ọnwa abụọ gachara, e tinyere ya n'ụlọ ọgwụ.

Taa, Musa bụ nwoke nke chọrọ ka o mara nke ọma. Nkwuputa a na-enye gị ihe ọmụma Musa chọrọ.

content.en:
SGBV stands for Sexual and Gender-Based Violence. It refers to any harmful act committed against a person's will, based on their gender or sex.

SGBV is not just physical beating. It includes: Physical violence (hitting, kicking, pushing). Sexual violence (rape, assault, harassment, unwanted touching). Emotional/psychological violence (threats, humiliation, control, isolation). Economic violence (controlling money, stopping someone from working). Harmful traditional practices (child marriage, FGM).

SGBV happens in homes, schools, workplaces, churches, mosques, and communities. It crosses every religion, tribe, and class.

Emotional/psychological violence (threats, humiliation, control, isolation). Economic violence (controlling money, stopping person from working). Harmful traditional practices (child marriage, FGM).

SGBV dey happen for homes, schools, workplaces, churches, mosques, and communities. E dey cross every religion, tribe, and class.
content.ha:
SGBV yana nufin Zaman Lafiya da Keta Hakkokin Jinsi. Yana nufin kowanne mummunan aiki da aka yi wa mutum ba tare da yardar sa ba, bisa ga jinsi ko jinsi.

SGBV ba kawai dukan jiki ba ne. Ya haɗa da: Zaman lafiyar jiki (dauka, duka, tura). Zaman lafiyar jima'i (kisa, hari, cin zarafi, taɓa ba tare da izini ba). Zaman lafiyar tunani/na hankali (barazanar, kunya, iko, keɓewa). Zaman lafiyar tattalin arziki (sarrafa kudi, hana mutum aiki). Mummunan al'adu (auren yara, FGM).

SGBV yana faruwa a gidaje, makarantu, wuraren aiki, coci, masallatai, da al'umma. Yana wuce kowanne addini, kabila, da ajin.
content.yo:
SGBV túmọ̀ sí Iwa-ibè àti Iwa-ibè ti Jinsi. Ó tọ́ka sí gbogbo ìṣe tó jẹ́ iparun tí a ṣe sí ẹnikan láì ní ìfaramọ́ wọn, da lori ìjìnlẹ̀ wọn tàbí ìjìnlẹ̀.

SGBV kì í ṣe dákẹ́dá jù. Ó ní: Iwa-ibè ti ara (ìkà, ìkà, ìtẹ́). Iwa-ibè ti jima (ìkà, ìkà, ìkà, ìtẹ́). Iwa-ibè ti ẹ̀mí/ìmọ̀ (ìkà, ìkà, ìkà, ìtẹ́). Iwa-ibè ti ọrọ̀ (ìṣàkóso owó, ìdènà ẹnikan láti ṣiṣẹ́). Àṣà tó jẹ́ iparun (ìyàwó ọmọ, FGM).

SGBV n ṣẹlẹ̀ ní ilé, ilé ẹ̀kọ́, ibi iṣẹ́, ṣọ́ọ̀ṣì, masalá, àti àwùjọ. Ó kọja gbogbo ẹ̀sìn, ìran, àti ìpò.
content.ig:
SGBV pụtara Iwu na Iwu nke Jinsi. Ọ na-ezo aka na omume ọjọọ ọ bụla e mere megide ọchịchọ onye, dabere na ụdị ma ọ bụ okike ha.

SGBV abụghị naanị ịkụ. Ọ na-agụnye: Iwu anụ ahụ (ịkụ, ịkụ, ịdọ). Iwu mmekọahụ (ịkpa, ịkpọ, ịkpa, ịkpọghị). Iwu mmetụta/psychological (ịkpa, ihere, njikwa, ịkpa). Iwu akụ na ụba (ijikwa ego, igbochi onye ka ọ rụọ ọrụ). Omume ọdịnala na-emebi (ịlụ di na nwunye na ụmụaka, FGM).

SGBV na-eme na ụlọ, ụlọ akwụkwọ, ebe ọrụ, ụka, masjid, na obodo. Ọ na-agafe okpukpe, agbụrụ, na klaasị niile.

content.en:
SGBV affects mostly women and girls — but not exclusively.

In Nigeria: 1 in 3 women have experienced physical violence. 1 in 4 girls are married before age 18. Boys and men can also be victims — especially of sexual violence and emotional abuse.

SGBV is not caused by what someone wears, where they go, or how they behave. It is caused by the person who chooses to commit violence. Victims are never to blame.

SGBV yana shafar mafi yawan mata da 'yan mata — amma ba su kadai ba ne.

A Najeriya: 1 cikin 3 mata sun fuskanci zaman lafiyar jiki. 1 cikin 4 'yan mata suna aure kafin su kai shekaru 18. Yara da maza ma na iya zama masu shafa — musamman na zaman lafiyar jima'i da cin zarafi na tunani.

SGBV ba ya faruwa saboda abin da mutum ke sawa, inda suke zuwa, ko yadda suke yi. Ana haifar da shi ne daga wanda ya zaɓi yin tashin hankali. Masu shafa ba su da laifi.

Ní Nàìjíríà: 1 nínú 3 obìnrin ti ní iriri iwa-ibè ti ara. 1 nínú 4 ọmọbìnrin ni a fẹ́yà ní kíkọ́ ọjọ́ 18. Àwọn ọmọkùnrin àti àwọn ọkùnrin tún lè jẹ́ olùṣàkóso — pàápàá jùlọ ti iwa-ibè ti jima àti iwa-ibè ti ẹ̀mí.

SGBV kì í ṣe nitori ohun tí ẹnikan wọ̀, ibè tí wọn lọ, tàbí bí wọn ṣe n hù. Ó jẹ́ nitori ẹni tó yan láti ṣe iwa-ibè. Àwọn olùṣàkóso kì í ṣe ẹ̀sùn.
content.ig:
SGBV na-emetụta ndị inyom na ụmụ agbọghọ karịsịa — ma ọ bụghị naanị ha.

Na Naijiria: 1 n'ime 3 ụmụ nwanyị enweela ahụhụ anụ ahụ. 1 n'ime 4 ụmụ agbọghọ lụrụ di tupu afọ 18. Nwoke na ụmụ nwoke nwekwara ike ịbụ ndị a na-emebi — karịsịa nke iwu mmekọahụ na iwere mmadụ n'obi.

SGBV abụghị n'ihi ihe onye na-eyi, ebe ha na-aga, ma ọ bụ otú ha si emekọrịta. Ọ bụ n'ihi onye họọrọ ime ihe ọjọọ. Ndị a na-emebi abụghị ndị na-emehie.

content.en:
SGBV does not just hurt the person it happens to. It damages entire communities.

Effects on survivors: Physical injuries (sometimes permanent). Mental health damage — depression, PTSD, anxiety, suicidal thoughts. Economic loss — inability to work or study. Social isolation — shame, stigma, silence.

Effects on communities: Broken families. Lower school enrollment for girls. Reduced productivity and economic growth. Cycles of violence passing from generation to generation.

Silence protects violence. Knowledge breaks that silence.

SGBV ba ya cutar da mutum kawai. Yana lalata dukkan al'umma.

Tasirin ga masu tsira: Raunin jiki (wannan yana iya zama na dindindin). Lalacewar lafiyar hankali — damuwa, PTSD, damuwa, tunanin kisan kai. Asarar tattalin arziki — rashin iya aiki ko karatu. Keɓewa na zamantakewa — kunya, stigma, shiru.

Tasirin ga al'umma: Rushewar iyalai. Rage rajistar makaranta ga 'yan mata. Rage yawan aiki da ci gaban tattalin arziki. Zaman lafiyar da ke wucewa daga ƙarni zuwa ƙarni.

Shiru yana kare tashin hankali. Ilimi yana karya wannan shiru.
content.yo:
SGBV kì í ṣe pé ó kan ẹni tó ṣẹlẹ̀ sí. Ó n pa gbogbo àwùjọ run.

Ìpa lórí àwọn tó yá: Iwariri ara (nígbà míì pẹ̀lú). Iwariri ilera ọpọlọ — ìbànújẹ, PTSD, ìbànújẹ, ìrònú ikú. Ìpadà owó — àìní láti ṣiṣẹ́ tàbí kẹ́kọ̀ọ́. Iṣọkan àwùjọ — ìkà, stigma, ìdákẹ́jẹ.

Ìpa lórí àwùjọ: Ìdílé tí a fọ́. Kíkọ́ ilé ẹ̀kọ́ kéré fún àwọn ọmọbìnrin. Ìdinku iṣẹ́ ati ìdàgbàsókè ọrọ̀ ajé. Àwọn ìkànsí iwa-ibè tí n kọja láti ìran sí ìran.

Ìdákẹ́jẹ n daabobo iwa-ibè. Ìmọ̀ n bọ́ sí i.
content.ig:
SGBV abụghị naanị na-emebi onye a na-eme ya. Ọ na-emebi obodo niile.

Nkwupụta na ndị na-ebi: Mmerụ ahụ (n'ọnọdụ ụfọdụ na-adịgide adịgide). Mmerụ ahụ na ahụike uche — ịda mbà, PTSD, nchekasị, echiche ịkpa. Mfu akụ na ụba — enweghị ike ịrụ ọrụ ma ọ bụ ịmụ. Ichebe onwe — ihere, stigma, ịdọpụ.

Nkwupụta na obodo: Ezinụlọ gbajiri agbaji. Nchekwa ụlọ akwụkwọ na ụmụ agbọghọ. Nchekwa na mmepe akụ na ụba. Ncheta nke iwa-ibè na-apụta site na ọgbọ ruo ọgbọ.

Ichebe onwe na-echebe iwa-ibè. Ihe ọmụma na-emebi nke a.

opening_story.en:
Meet the Adeyemi household.

Mr. Adeyemi earns all the money. Mrs. Adeyemi stays home with the children. When she asks for money to buy food, he says: "Whose money is it? You will use it as I say."

Their son, Junior, watches everything. He is 8 years old.

By the time Junior is 25, he believes that a man's money gives him the right to control a woman's body, movement, and voice.

Junior never hit anyone. But he controls his girlfriend's phone. He decides where she can go. He monitors her friends.

Junior learned this. Not from evil — but from what he watched every day growing up.

Today we trace the roots.

opening_story.ha:
Gane iyalan Adeyemi.

Mr. Adeyemi yana samun dukkan kudin. Mrs. Adeyemi tana gida tare da yara. Lokacin da ta nemi kudi don sayen abinci, yana cewa: "Wane kudi ne? Za ki yi amfani da shi kamar yadda na ce."

Yaransu, Junior, yana kallon komai. Yana da shekaru 8.

A lokacin da Junior ya kai shekaru 25, yana yarda cewa kudi na namiji yana ba shi hakkin sarrafa jikin mace, motsi, da murya.

Junior ba ya taba dukan kowa. Amma yana sarrafa wayar budurwarsa. Yana yanke shawarar inda za ta tafi. Yana lura da abokanta.

Junior ya koya wannan. Ba daga mugunta ba — amma daga abin da ya kalli kowace rana yana girma.

A yau za mu bi asalin.
opening_story.yo:
Ẹ jọ̀ọ́, ẹ jẹ́ ká mọ́ ìdílé Adeyemi.

Mr. Adeyemi ni ẹni tó ń rí gbogbo owó. Mrs. Adeyemi ń bẹ ní ilé pẹ̀lú àwọn ọmọ. Nígbà tí ó bá béèrè owó láti ra oúnjẹ, ó máa sọ pé: "Tani owó yìí? Iwọ yóò lo ó gẹ́gẹ́ bí mo ṣe sọ."

Ọmọ wọn, Junior, ń wo gbogbo nkan. Ó ní ọdún 8.

Nígbà tí Junior bá ti pé ọdún 25, ó ní ìgbàgbọ́ pé owó ọkùnrin ni yóò fún un ní ẹ̀tọ́ láti ṣàkóso ara obìnrin, ìrìn, àti ohùn.

Junior kò tíì kọ́ ẹnikẹ́ni. Ṣùgbọ́n ó ń ṣàkóso foonu ìyàwó rẹ. Ó pinnu ibi tí ó lè lọ. Ó ń tọ́pa àwọn ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ.

Junior kọ́ ẹ̀kọ́ yìí. Kò jẹ́ láti inú ibi — ṣùgbọ́n láti ohun tó ń wo ní gbogbo ọjọ́ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ó ṣe ń dàgbà.

Lónìí, a máa tọ́pa ìdí rẹ.
opening_story.ig:
Nabata ezinụlọ Adeyemi.

Mr. Adeyemi na-enweta ego niile. Mrs. Adeyemi nọ n'ụlọ na ụmụaka. Mgbe ọ na-arịọ ego iji zụta nri, ọ na-ekwu: "Kedu ego nke a? Ị ga-eji ya dịka m kwuru."

Nwa ha, Junior, na-ele anya na ihe niile. Ọ bụ afọ 8.

Mgbe Junior ruru afọ 25, ọ kwenyere na ego nwoke na-enye ya ikike ịchịkwa ahụ nwanyị, mmegharị, na olu.

Junior adịghị akpọrọ onye ọ bụla. Ma ọ na-achịkwa ekwentị enyi ya. Ọ na-ekpebi ebe ọ ga-aga. Ọ na-enyocha ndị enyi ya.

Junior mụtara nke a. Ọ bụghị site na ihe ọjọọ — kama site na ihe ọ na-ahụ kwa ụbọchị na-eto eto.

Taa, anyị ga-achọpụta isi mkpụrụ.

content.en:
The single biggest root cause of SGBV is unequal power — when one person believes they have the right to control, own, or dominate another.

Power imbalances show up as: Economic power ("I earn the money, so I decide everything"). Physical power (using size or strength to intimidate). Social power (using status or title to silence others). Institutional power (when laws and systems protect abusers, not survivors).

Where there is unchecked power, abuse follows. Not always. But far too often.

content.ha:
Babban asalin dalilin SGBV shine rashin daidaito na iko — lokacin da mutum daya ya yarda cewa yana da hakkin sarrafa, mallaka, ko mulkin wani.

Rashin daidaito na iko yana bayyana a matsayin: Ikon tattalin arziki ("Ni nake samun kudin, don haka ni nake yanke shawara akan komai"). Ikon jiki (amfani da girma ko karfi don tsoratarwa). Ikon zamantakewa (amfani da matsayi ko suna don shushugawa wasu). Ikon hukumomi (lokacin da dokoki da tsarin suke kare masu zalunci, ba masu tsira ba).

Inda akwai iko mara iyaka, zalunci yana biyo baya. Ba koyaushe ba. Amma yana faruwa sosai.
content.yo:
Ìdí tó pọ̀ jùlọ tí SGBV fi wà ni àìdá iko — nígbà tí ènìyàn kan bá ní ìgbàgbọ́ pé ó ní ẹ̀tọ́ láti ṣàkóso, ní, tàbí kó àwọn míì.

Àìdá iko ń hàn gẹ́gẹ́ bí: Iko ìṣúná ("Mo ń rí owó, nítorí náà, èmi ni yóò pinnu gbogbo nkan"). Iko ara (lilo ìwọn tàbí agbára láti fa ẹ̀rù). Iko awujọ (lilo ipo tàbí akọ́lé láti dákẹ́ ẹlòmíì). Iko ilé iṣẹ́ (nígbà tí òfin àti àwọn eto ń daabobo àwọn tó ń ṣe ìkà, kì í ṣe àwọn tó ti gbà á).

Níbi tí kò sí àìdá iko, ìkà ń tẹ̀síwájú. Kò jẹ́ pé gbogbo ìgbà. Ṣùgbọ́n ó ṣẹlẹ̀ púpọ̀.
content.ig:
Isi mkpụrụ nke SGBV bụ enweghị ntụkwasị obi — mgbe otu onye kwenyere na ọ nwere ikike ịchịkwa, inwe, ma ọ bụ ịchịkwa onye ọzọ.

Nchekwa iwu na-apụta dị ka: Iwu akụ na ụba ("Anọ m na-enweta ego, ya mere, m na-ekpebi ihe niile"). Iwu anụ ahụ (iji nha ma ọ bụ ike mee ka mmadụ nwee egwu). Iwu mmekọrịta (iji ọnọdụ ma ọ bụ aha mee ka ndị ọzọ kwụsị). Iwu ụlọ ọrụ (mgbe iwu na usoro na-echebe ndị na-eme ihe ọjọọ, ọ bụghị ndị na-eto eto).

N'ebe a na-enweghị nchebe iwu, mmegbu na-esochi. Ọ bụghị mgbe niile. Ma ọ na-eme ọtụtụ oge.

content.en:
Culture shapes what we believe is normal. Socialisation is how those beliefs are passed on — through family, religion, media, peers, and community.

In many Nigerian communities, culture teaches: that men are naturally dominant; that women must be submissive and silent; that family matters must stay private; that a man's authority is sacred.

These teachings are not facts. They are traditions. And traditions can be examined, challenged, and changed.

Culture is powerful. But it is also made by people — and can be remade by people.
content.pcm:
Culture dey shape wetin we believe say na normal. Socialisation na how dem dey pass those beliefs — through family, religion, media, peers, and community.

For many Nigerian communities, culture dey teach: say men dey naturally dominant; say women suppose dey submissive and silent; say family matter suppose dey private; say a man authority na sacred.

These teachings no be facts. Dem na traditions. And traditions fit dey examined, challenged, and changed.

Culture dey powerful. But e still dey made by people — and fit be remade by people.
content.ha:
Al'adu suna tsara abin da muke yarda da shi a matsayin na al'ada. Hanyoyin zamani shine yadda ake watsawa waɗannan imani — ta hanyar iyali, addini, kafofin watsa labarai, abokai, da al'umma.

A cikin yawancin al'ummomin Najeriya, al'adu suna koyarwa: cewa maza suna da iko na halitta; cewa mata dole ne su zama masu biyayya da shiru; cewa al'amuran iyali dole ne su kasance na sirri; cewa ikon namiji na da tsarki.

Wannan koyarwar ba gaskiya bane. Su al'adu ne. Kuma al'adu za a iya duba su, kalubalantar su, da canza su.

Al'adu suna da karfi. Amma ana kuma yin su daga mutane — kuma za a iya sake yin su daga mutane.
content.yo:
Àṣà ń dá ohun tí a ní ìgbàgbọ́ pé ó jẹ́ àṣà. Ìkànsí ni bí wọ́n ṣe ń kọ́ àwọn ìgbàgbọ́ wọ̀lú — nípasẹ̀ ìdílé, ẹ̀sìn, ìkànnì, àwọn ọ̀rẹ́, àti àjọṣe.

Nínú ọ̀pọ̀ àwùjọ Nàìjíríà, àṣà ń kọ́: pé àwọn ọkùnrin ni wọ́n jẹ́ alákóso; pé àwọn obìnrin gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ aláìlera àti dákẹ́; pé àwọn ìṣòro ìdílé gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ ìkọ̀kọ́; pé àṣẹ ọkùnrin jẹ́ mímọ́.

Àwọn ẹ̀kọ́ wọ̀nyí kì í ṣe òtítọ́. Wọ́n jẹ́ àṣà. Àti pé àṣà lè jẹ́ àyẹ̀wò, ìdáhùn, àti yípadà.

Àṣà ní agbára. Ṣùgbọ́n ó tún jẹ́ ti àwọn ènìyàn — àti pé a lè tún ṣe é nípasẹ̀ àwọn ènìyàn.
content.ig:
Omume na-emepụta ihe anyị kwenyere na ọ bụ ihe a na-ahụkarị. Ncheta bụ otú a na-esi ewere ndị a kwenyere — site na ezinụlọ, okpukperechi, mgbasa ozi, ndị enyi, na obodo.

N'ógbè Nigeria, omenaala na-akụziri: na ndị nwoke bụ ndị nwere ikike; na ndị nwanyị ga-abụ ndị na-anaghị ekwu ma na-ezobe; na ihe gbasara ezinụlọ ga-anọpụ iche; na ikike nwoke bụ nke a na-asọpụrụ.

A na-akụziri ndị a abụghị eziokwu. Ha bụ omenala. Na omenala nwere ike ịtụle, ịjụ ajụjụ, na ịgbanwe.

Omenala nwere ike. Ma ọ bụkwa nke ndị mmadụ — ma nwee ike ịmegharị site n'aka ndị mmadụ.

content.en:
Poverty and economic inequality create conditions where SGBV can thrive.

When a woman has no income, no savings, and no access to resources, she may feel trapped in an abusive relationship with no way out.

When a man faces unemployment and financial failure, and his identity is built entirely on "being the provider," the shame can turn into aggression.

Economic exclusion of women from education and financial independence is a structural driver of gender-based violence. Ending SGBV means also fighting for economic justice.
content.pcm:
Poverty and economic inequality dey create conditions wey SGBV fit thrive.

When woman no get income, no savings, and no access to resources, she fit dey feel trapped for abusive relationship with no way out.

When man dey face unemployment and financial failure, and him identity dey built entirely on "being the provider," the shame fit turn to aggression.

Economic exclusion of women from education and financial independence na structural driver of gender-based violence. To end SGBV mean say we go dey fight for economic justice.
content.ha:
Talauci da rashin daidaito na tattalin arziki suna haifar da yanayi inda SGBV zai iya bunƙasa.

Lokacin da mace ba ta da kudin shiga, babu ajiyar kudi, kuma babu damar samun albarkatu, tana iya jin cewa an kulle ta a cikin dangantaka mai cutarwa ba tare da hanyar fita ba.

Lokacin da namiji ke fuskantar rashin aikin yi da gazawar kudi, kuma ainihin sa an gina shi gaba ɗaya akan "zama mai bayarwa," kunya na iya zama tashin hankali.

Rashin samun ilimi da 'yancin kudi ga mata yana zama tushen tsarin zalunci na jinsi. Kammala SGBV yana nufin kuma yaƙi don adalcin tattalin arziki.
content.yo:
Iṣoro àti àìdá ìṣúná ń dá àwọn ipo tí SGBV lè yá.

Nígbà tí obìnrin kò ní owó, kò ní àpò, àti kò ní iraye sí àwọn oríṣìíríṣìí, ó lè ní ìmọ̀lára pé a ti pa a mọ́ nínú ìbáṣepọ̀ tó ní ìkà.

Nígbà tí ọkùnrin bá dojú kọ́ àìní iṣẹ́ àti ìkuna owó, àti pé ìdí rẹ̀ ti dá lórí "jijẹ́ olùpèsè," ìtìjú lè yí padà sí ìkà.

Àìní obìnrin láti kó ẹ̀kọ́ àti ìyàtọ̀ owó jẹ́ olùmúlò àìdá ìkà. Kí a parí SGBV túmọ̀ sí pé a tún ní láti ja fún ìdájọ́ ìṣúná.
content.ig:
Ihughari na enweghị ntụkwasị obi akụ na ụba na-emepụta ọnọdụ ebe SGBV nwere ike ịbawanye.

Mgbe nwanyị enweghị ego, enweghị nchekwa, na enweghị ohere ịnweta ihe, ọ nwere ike ịnụ na ọ bụ n'ịbụ onye na-eme ihe ọjọọ na-enweghị ụzọ pụọ.

Mgbe nwoke na-eche ihu enweghị ọrụ na mmefu ego, na njirimara ya bụ naanị "inwe onye na-enye," ihere nwere ike ịgbanwe na mmegbu.

Iwepụ ndị nwanyị na agụmakwụkwọ na nnwere onwe akụ na ụba bụ ihe na-akpata mmegbu nke ụdị. Imechi SGBV pụtara ịlụso ọgụ maka eziokwu akụ na ụba.

opening_story.en:
Meet Tunde.

Tunde is 30. He works in a Lagos office. One afternoon, a colleague makes a degrading joke about a female colleague — the whole room laughs.

Tunde wants to speak. His heart is beating fast. But a voice in his head says: "Don't make it awkward. It's just a joke. Nobody will thank you."

He stays silent. But the woman he defended in his mind goes home that day feeling invisible.

Later that week, Tunde's younger sister tells him she is experiencing harassment at her job. She says no one speaks up for her.

Tunde sits quietly. And he realises: he was the type of person his sister was hoping for — and he chose silence.

This module is about choosing differently.
opening_story.pcm:
Meet Tunde.

Tunde dey 30. E dey work for one office for Lagos. One afternoon, one colleague crack joke wey dey shame woman wey dey work with dem — everybody for the room dey laugh.

Tunde wan talk. Him heart dey beat fast. But one voice for him head dey tell am: "No go make am awkward. Na just joke. Nobody go thank you."

E keep quiet. But the woman wey him defend for him mind go house that day dey feel invisible.

Later that week, Tunde younger sister tell am say she dey experience harassment for her job. She talk say nobody dey speak for her.

Tunde dey sit down quietly. And him realize say: na him type of person wey him sister dey hope for — and him choose silence.

This module na about choosing differently.
opening_story.ha:
Gane Tunde.

Tunde yana da shekaru 30. Yana aiki a ofishin Lagos. Wata rana, wani abokin aiki ya yi wani barkwanci mai zagi game da wata mata — dukkanin dakin suna dariya.

Tunde yana son magana. Zuciyarsa na bugawa da sauri. Amma wata murya a cikin kansa tana cewa: "Kada ka sa ya zama ba daidai ba. Barkwancin ne kawai. Ba wanda zai gode maka."

Ya zauna shiru. Amma matar da ya kare a cikin tunaninsa ta tafi gida a ranar tana jin kamar ba a ganinta.

Bayan wannan makon, kanwarsa ta gaya masa tana fuskantar cin zarafi a aikinta. Ta ce babu wanda ke magana a madadinta.

Tunde ya zauna cikin shiru. Kuma ya fahimci: shine irin mutumin da kanwarsa ke fata — kuma ya zabi shiru.

Wannan module yana magana ne akan zabar daban.
opening_story.yo:
Pẹ̀lú Tunde.

Tunde jẹ́ ọmọ ọdún 30. Ó ń ṣiṣẹ́ ní ọ́fíìsì kan ní Lagos. Ọjọ́ kan, ẹlẹ́gbẹ́ kan ṣe ẹ̀rín tó ní ìkànsí nípa obìnrin kan — gbogbo ilé náà ń rẹ́rìn-ín.

Tunde fẹ́ sọ̀rọ̀. Ọkàn rẹ̀ ń bù kó. Ṣùgbọ́n ohùn kan nínú rẹ sọ pé: "Má ṣe jẹ́ kó di ìbànújẹ. Kò jẹ́ ẹ̀rín. Kò sí ẹnìkan tó máa dupẹ́ fún ọ."

Ó pa ẹnu mọ́. Ṣùgbọ́n obìnrin tí ó dáàbò bo nínú ìmọ̀ rẹ̀ lọ sí ilé ní ọjọ́ yẹn ní ìmọ̀lára pé kò sí ẹnìkan tó rí i.

Ní ọjọ́ yẹn, ìyàwó Tunde sọ fún un pé ó ń ní ìkànsí níbi iṣẹ́ rẹ. Ó sọ pé kò sí ẹnìkan tó ń sọ̀rọ̀ fún un.

Tunde jókòó ní ìkànsí. Ó sì mọ̀ pé: ó jẹ́ irú ènìyàn tí ìyàwó rẹ̀ ń retí — ó sì yan ìkànsí.

Module yìí jẹ́ nípa yíyan ní ìtọ́ka.
opening_story.ig:
Nwee Tunde.

Tunde bụ afọ 30. Ọ na-arụ ọrụ na ọfịs Lagos. Otu ehihie, onye ọrụ ibe ya mere ihe na-adịghị mma banyere nwanyị ọrụ ibe ha — ụlọ niile na-eme ọchị.

Tunde chọrọ ikwu. Obi ya na-ama ọsọ. Ma ụda dị na uche ya na-ekwu: "Ekwela ka ọ bụrụ ihe na-adịghị mma. Ọ bụ naanị ihe ọchị. Ọ dịghị onye ga-eke gị ekele."

O nọrọ n'udo. Ma nwanyị ọ na-echebe na uche ya gara n'ụlọ n'ehihie ahụ na-enwe mmetụta na ọ bụghị onye a hụrụ.

N'ikpeazụ izu ahụ, nwanne Tunde na-agwa ya na ọ na-enwe nsogbu na ọrụ ya. Ọ na-ekwu na ọ dịghị onye na-ekwu maka ya.

Tunde nọ n'udo. Ọ na-amata: ọ bụ ụdị mmadụ nwanne ya na-atụ anya — ma o họrọ n'udo.

Module a bụ banyere ịhọrọ nke ọzọ.

content.en:
For too long, gender-based violence has been framed as "a women's issue." This is wrong — and dangerous.

Men commit the vast majority of GBV. Men hold most social, economic, and political power. And men have enormous influence over other men.

This means men are not just part of the problem. Men are essential to the solution.

When a man speaks up, other men listen in ways they don't when women speak. That influence is powerful — and carries responsibility.
content.pcm:
For too long, dem don frame gender-based violence as "women matter." This one no correct — and e dey dangerous.

Men dey commit plenty GBV. Men dey hold most social, economic, and political power. And men get plenty influence over other men.

This mean say men no be just part of the problem. Men dey essential to the solution.

When man talk, other men dey listen in ways wey dem no dey listen when women dey talk. That influence dey powerful — and e carry responsibility.
content.ha:
Har yanzu, an dauki tashin hankali na jinsi a matsayin "lamarin mata." Wannan ba daidai ba ne — kuma yana da hadari.

Maza suna aikata yawancin tashin hankali na jinsi. Maza suna da mafi yawan iko na zamantakewa, tattalin arziki, da siyasa. Kuma maza suna da tasiri mai yawa akan sauran maza.

Wannan yana nufin maza ba kawai suna cikin matsalar ba. Maza suna da mahimmanci ga maganin.

Lokacin da namijin ya yi magana, sauran maza suna sauraron hanyoyin da ba sa sauraron lokacin da mata suka yi magana. Wannan tasirin yana da karfi — kuma yana dauke da alhakin.
content.yo:
Fún pẹ́lú, ìkànsí tó dá lórí ìbáṣepọ̀ ti wa níbi tí a ti kà á sí "ìṣòro obìnrin." Èyí jẹ́ aṣiṣe — àti pé ó lewu.

Àwọn ọkùnrin ni wọ́n ń ṣe àkúnya tó pọ̀ jùlọ nínú ìkànsí. Àwọn ọkùnrin ni wọ́n ní agbára tó pọ̀ jùlọ nínú awujọ, ọrọ̀ ajé, àti ìṣèlú. Àti pé àwọn ọkùnrin ni wọ́n ní ipa tó lágbára lórí àwọn ọkùnrin míì.

Èyí túmọ̀ sí pé àwọn ọkùnrin kì í ṣe apá kan ṣoṣo nínú ìṣòro. Àwọn ọkùnrin jẹ́ pataki sí ìpinnu.

Nígbà tí ọkùnrin bá sọ̀rọ̀, àwọn ọkùnrin míì ń tẹ́tí sí i ní ọ̀nà tí wọ́n kò tẹ́tí sí i nígbà tí àwọn obìnrin bá sọ̀rọ̀. Ipa yẹn jẹ́ alágbára — àti pé ó ní ojúṣe.
content.ig:
Ruo ogologo oge, a na-atụle mmegbu nke mmekọahụ dịka "ihe ụmụ nwanyị." Nke a bụ ihe na-ezighị ezi — na ihe ize ndụ.

Ndị ikpọrọ na-eme ọtụtụ mmegbu nke mmekọahụ. Ndị ikpọrọ nwere ọtụtụ ikike mmekọrịta, akụ na ụba, na ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị. Na ndị ikpọrọ nwere nnukwu mmetụta n'elu ndị ikpọrọ ndị ọzọ.

Nke a pụtara na ndị ikpọrọ abụghị naanị akụkụ nke nsogbu. Ndị ikpọrọ dị mkpa na ngwọta.

Mgbe nwoke na-ekwu, ndị ikpọrọ ndị ọzọ na-ege ntị n'ụzọ ha na-ege ntị na ụmụ nwanyị na-ekwu. Mmetụta ahụ bụ ihe dị ike — na-ewepụta ọrụ.

content.en:
Being an ally means actively using your position and voice to support those who are being harmed. Allyship is not just "not being abusive." It is taking action.

Practical allyship: Speaking up when you hear a sexist joke. Refusing to laugh at content that mocks women. Supporting a friend you think is being abused. Calling out a friend when his behaviour is controlling. Modelling respectful relationships in your own life.

Allyship is not a performance. It is a daily practice.
content.pcm:
To be ally mean say you dey actively use your position and voice to support those wey dey suffer. Allyship no be just "no dey abusive." Na to take action.

Practical allyship: To speak up when you hear sexist joke. To refuse to laugh at content wey dey mock women. To support friend wey you think dey suffer abuse. To call out friend when him behavior dey controlling. To model respectful relationships for your own life.

Allyship no be performance. Na daily practice.
content.ha:
Zama aboki yana nufin amfani da matsayin ka da murya don tallafawa wadanda ake cutarwa. Allyship ba kawai "ba a yi tashin hankali ba." Yana nufin daukar mataki.

Allyship mai amfani: Yin magana lokacin da ka ji barkwanci mai zagi. Kin dariya akan abubuwan da ke zagi mata. Tallafawa aboki da kake tunanin ana cutar da shi. Kiran aboki lokacin da halayensa ke zama masu iko. Nuna kyawawan dangantaka a rayuwarka.

Allyship ba aikin kwaikwayo bane. Yana da aikin yau da kullum.
content.yo:
Jẹ́ alágbàdo túmọ̀ sí pé o ń lo ipo rẹ àti ohùn rẹ láti ṣe atilẹyin fún àwọn tó ń jiya. Allyship kì í ṣe "kì í ṣe ìkànsí." Ó jẹ́ láti ṣe ìgbésẹ̀.

Allyship tó wúlò: Sọ̀rọ̀ nígbà tí o bá gbọ́ ẹ̀rín tó ní ìkànsí. Kí o má ṣe rẹ́rìn-ín sí ohun tó ń zà obìnrin. Ṣe atilẹyin fún ọ̀rẹ́ kan tí o ro pé ó ń jiya. Pe ọ̀rẹ́ kan nígbà tí ìhùwàsí rẹ̀ bá jẹ́ alágbára. Fi àpẹẹrẹ ìbáṣepọ̀ tó ní ìbáṣepọ̀ rere hàn nínú ìgbé ayé rẹ.

Allyship kì í ṣe ìṣe àfihàn. Ó jẹ́ ìṣe ojoojúmọ́.
content.ig:
Iji bụrụ onye na-akwado pụtara na ị na-eji ọnọdụ gị na olu gị kwado ndị na-enweta ihe mgbu. Allyship abụghị naanị "ịbụ onye na-emeghị mmegbu." Ọ bụ ịme ihe.

Allyship bara uru: Ikwu mgbe ị na-anụ ihe ọchị na-eme ihe na-adịghị mma. Iji gbochie ịchị ọchị na ọdịnaya na-eme ihe na-adịghị mma na ụmụ nwanyị. Ikwado enyi ị na-eche na a na-eme ya ihe. Kpọọ enyi mgbe omume ya na-achịkwa. Ime ihe atụ nke mmekọrịta na-enwe nkwanye ugwu n'ime ndụ gị.

Allyship abụghị ihe ngosi. Ọ bụ omume kwa ụbọchị.

content.en:
Change starts with you. Not with the government. Not with a campaign. With the choices you make every single day.

Your personal responsibility includes: Examining your own behaviours and attitudes honestly. Recognising how you may have benefited from gender inequality. Making a commitment — not just to avoid harm, but to actively prevent it. Holding yourself accountable when you fall short.

Nobody is perfect. But everyone can improve. And every improvement matters.
content.pcm:
Change dey start with you. No be with government. No be with campaign. Na with the choices wey you dey make every single day.

Your personal responsibility include: To examine your own behaviors and attitudes honestly. To recognize how you fit don benefit from gender inequality. To make commitment — no be just to avoid harm, but to actively prevent am. To hold yourself accountable when you fall short.

Nobody dey perfect. But everybody fit improve. And every improvement matter.
content.ha:
Canji yana farawa daga gare ku. Ba daga gwamnati ba. Ba daga kamfen ba. Daga zaɓin da kuke yi kowace rana.

Alhakin ku na kai ya haɗa da: Duba halayen ku da ra'ayoyin ku da gaskiya. Gane yadda zaku iya amfana daga rashin daidaito na jinsi. Yin alkawari — ba kawai don guje wa cutarwa ba, amma don hana ta a zahiri. Rike kanku da alhakin lokacin da kuka gaza.

Babu wanda ya zama cikakke. Amma kowa na iya inganta. Kuma kowanne ingantawa yana da mahimmanci.
content.yo:
Ayipada bẹ̀rẹ̀ pẹ̀lú rẹ. Kò sí pẹ̀lú ìjọba. Kò sí pẹ̀lú ipolongo. Pẹ̀lú àwọn yiyan tí o ṣe ní gbogbo ọjọ́.

Ojuse ara rẹ ni: Ṣàkíyèsí ìhùwàsí rẹ àti ìmọ̀ràn rẹ ní ìtẹ́lọ́run. Mọ̀ pé bí o ṣe lè ti ní anfaani láti ìbáṣepọ̀ tó kì í ṣe dọ́gba. Ṣe ìlérí — kì í ṣe láti yago fún ìkànsí, ṣùgbọ́n láti ṣe àtìlẹ́yìn rẹ. Dà á sílẹ̀ fún ara rẹ nígbà tí o bá ṣàì ṣeé ṣe.

Kò sí ẹnìkan tó péye. Ṣùgbọ́n gbogbo ènìyàn lè ṣe àtúnṣe. Àti pé gbogbo àtúnṣe ní ìtàn.
content.ig:
Mgbanwe na-amalite na gị. Ọ bụghị na ọchịchị. Ọ bụghị na mgbasa ozi. Na nhọrọ ị na-eme kwa ụbọchị.

Ọrụ gị n'ịbụ onye nwe gụnyere: Nyocha omume gị na echiche gị n'eziokwu. Ịmata otú ị nwere ike inwe uru site na inequality mmekọahụ. Ịme nkwa — ọ bụghị naanị izere mmegbu, ma na-eme ka ọ ghara ime. Iji jide onwe gị na ọrụ mgbe ị na-ezighị ezi.

Enweghị onye zuru oke. Ma onye ọ bụla nwere ike imeziwanye. Na mmezi ọ bụla dị mkpa.

opening_story.en:
Meet Emeka again.

Emeka has been learning. He is now in a relationship with Adaeze, a woman he deeply respects.

But he is confused about some things. When he is stressed, he shuts down and goes silent. Adaeze says he makes her feel invisible.

One evening, they have a disagreement. Emeka raises his voice. Adaeze flinches.

He sees her flinch. And for the first time, he really sees it.

He sits down. He breathes. And he says: "I'm sorry. Can we start again?"

That moment changes everything. Today, we talk about what healthy relationships actually look like — and the skills that build them.
opening_story.pcm:
Meet Emeka again.

Emeka don dey learn. Him don enter relationship with Adaeze, one woman wey him dey respect well well.

But him dey confused about some things. When stress don catch am, him go just shut down and dey silent. Adaeze dey talk say him dey make her feel invisible.

One evening, dem get wahala. Emeka raise him voice. Adaeze flinch.

Him see as she flinch. And for the first time, him really see am.

Him sit down. Him breathe. And him talk: "I’m sorry. Fit we start again?"

That moment change everything. Today, we go talk about wetin healthy relationships really be like — and the skills wey go build am.
opening_story.ha:
Sadu Emeka a sake.

Emeka yana koyon. Yanzu yana cikin dangantaka da Adaeze, wata mace da yake girmama sosai.

Amma yana cikin rudani game da wasu abubuwa. Lokacin da yake cikin damuwa, yana rufewa da shiru. Adaeze tana cewa yana sa ta ji kamar ba ta da mahimmanci.

Wata yamma, suna samun sabani. Emeka ya daga murya. Adaeze ta yi tsalle.

Ya ga ta yi tsalle. Kuma a karo na farko, ya ga shi sosai.

Ya zauna. Ya yi numfashi. Kuma ya ce: "Yi hakuri. Za mu iya farawa daga farko?"

Wannan lokacin ya canza komai. Yau, muna magana akan yadda dangantaka mai kyau take — da kuma kwarewar da ke gina su.
opening_story.yo:
Ẹ jẹ́ ká tún mọ Emeka.

Emeka ti ń kọ́ ẹ̀kọ́. Ó ti wà nínú ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú Adaeze, obìnrin tó ní ìbáṣepọ̀ pẹ̀lú.

Ṣùgbọ́n ó ní ìdààmú nípa àwọn nnkan kan. Nígbà tí ó bá ní ìṣòro, ó máa pa ara rẹ̀ mọ́, ó sì máa dáhùn. Adaeze sọ pé ó ń jẹ́ kí ó ní ìmọ̀lára pé kò sí.

Ní ọ̀sán kan, wọn ní ìfarapa. Emeka gbé ohùn rẹ̀ soke. Adaeze dáhùn.

Ó rí i pé ó dáhùn. Kò sì ní àkókò yìí, ó rí i gidi.

Ó jókòó. Ó mu afẹ́fẹ́. Ó sì sọ pé: "Mo bínú. Ṣé a lè bẹ̀rẹ̀ sí i tún?"

Àkókò yẹn yí gbogbo nkan padà. Lónìí, a máa sọ̀rọ̀ nípa bí ìbáṣepọ̀ tó dára ṣe rí — àti àwọn ọgbọn tó ń kọ́ wọn.
opening_story.ig:
Nabata Emeka ọzọ.

Emeka amalitela ịmụ. Ọ nọ na mmekọrịta na Adaeze, nwanyị ọ na-asọpụrụ nke ukwuu.

Ma ọ na-enwe mgbagwoju anya banyere ụfọdụ ihe. Mgbe ọ na-enwe nrụgide, ọ na-emechi onwe ya ma na-ada ụda. Adaeze na-ekwu na ọ na-eme ka ọ bụrụ onye na-adịghị ahụ anya.

Otu mgbede, ha nwere esemokwu. Emeka na-ebuli olu ya. Adaeze na-ama jijiji.

Ọ hụrụ ya na-ama jijiji. Ma maka oge mbụ, ọ hụrụ ya n'ezie.

Ọ na-anọdụ. Ọ na-ewepụ ume. Ọ na-ekwu: "Ekwela m. Anyị nwere ike ịmalite ọzọ?"

Oge ahụ gbanwere ihe niile. Taa, anyị na-ekwu maka otú mmekọrịta dị mma si dị — na nka ndị na-ewu ha.

content.en:
Consent means freely, enthusiastically, and clearly agreeing to something.

Consent must be: Freely given (not under pressure or fear). Reversible (a person can change their mind at any time). Informed (both people understand what they're agreeing to). Enthusiastic (an uncertain "yes" is not a full yes). Specific (saying yes to one thing does not mean yes to everything).

Consent applies to sex. But also to everyday decisions in relationships — where you go, who you see, what you share.

A relationship without consent is not a relationship. It is control.
content.pcm:
Consent na when person gree something freely, with joy, and clearly.

Consent suppose be: Freely given (no under pressure or fear). Reversible (person fit change him mind anytime). Informed (both people sabi wetin dem dey gree). Enthusiastic (one uncertain "yes" no be full yes). Specific (to say yes to one thing no mean yes to everything).

Consent dey apply to sex. But e dey apply to everyday decisions for relationships — where you go, who you see, wetin you share.

Relationship wey no get consent no be relationship. Na control.
content.ha:
Yarda na nufin yarda da wani abu cikin 'yanci, da sha'awa, da kuma a fili.

Yarda dole ne ta kasance: An bayar da 'yanci (ba a cikin matsin lamba ko tsoro). Ana iya janye (wani na iya canza ra'ayi a kowane lokaci). An san (dukkan mutane suna fahimtar abin da suke yarda da shi). Da sha'awa ("eh" mara tabbas ba cikakken eh ba ne). Musamman (yarda da abu guda ba yana nufin yarda da komai ba).

Yarda tana shafar jima'i. Amma kuma tana shafar yanke shawara na yau da kullum a cikin dangantaka — inda za ku tafi, wanda za ku gani, abin da za ku raba.

Dangantaka ba tare da yarda ba ba dangantaka ba ce. Tana nufin iko.
content.yo:
Ìfaramọ́ túmọ̀ sí kí ẹnikan gba nkan kan nífẹ̀ẹ́, ní ìfẹ́, àti ní kedere.

Ìfaramọ́ gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́: Kí a fi ẹ̀tọ́ sílẹ̀ (kò ní ìmúra tàbí ìbànújẹ). Kí a lè yí padà (ẹnikan lè yí ìmọ̀ràn rẹ̀ padà ní kankan). Kí a mọ̀ (mejeeji ní ìmọ̀ nípa ohun tí wọn ń gba). Kí a ní ìfẹ́ ("bẹ́ẹ̀ ni" tí kò dájú kì í ṣe "bẹ́ẹ̀ ni" gidi). Kí a jẹ́ kedere (nífẹẹ́ sí ohun kan kò túmọ̀ sí nífẹẹ́ sí gbogbo nkan).

Ìfaramọ́ ní í ṣe pẹ̀lú jímá. Ṣùgbọ́n ó tún ní í ṣe pẹ̀lú àwọn ìpinnu ojoojúmọ́ nínú ìbáṣepọ̀ — ibè wo ni ẹ̀, ta ni ẹ̀ ń rí, kí ni ẹ̀ ń pín.

Ìbáṣepọ̀ tí kò ní ìfaramọ́ kì í ṣe ìbáṣepọ̀. Ó jẹ́ ìṣàkóso.
content.ig:
Nkwenye pụtara ịkwenye ihe n'efu, n'ịhụnanya, na nke doro anya.

Nkwenye ga-abụ: N'efu (ọ bụghị n'okpuru nrụgide ma ọ bụ egwu). N'ịgbanwe (onye nwere ike ịgbanwe echiche ha n'oge ọ bụla). N'ịmara (ma ndị mmadụ abụọ na-aghọta ihe ha na-akwado). N'ịhụnanya ("ee" na-adịghị doro anya abụghị "ee" zuru ezu). N'ịkọwa (ịsị ee na otu ihe apụtaghị ee na ihe niile).

Nkwenye na-emetụta mmekọrịta. Ma ọ na-emetụta mkpebi kwa ụbọchị na mmekọrịta — ebe ị na-aga, onye ị na-ahụ, ihe ị na-ekekọrịta.

Mmekọrịta na-enweghị nkwenye abụghị mmekọrịta. Ọ bụ njikwa.

content.en:
Healthy relationships require honest, respectful communication — especially during conflict.

Signs of healthy communication: Listening to understand, not just to respond. Expressing feelings without blame ("I feel..." not "You always..."). Taking responsibility for your own emotions. Being willing to take a break when conversations get too heated.

Signs of unhealthy communication: Shouting, threatening, or using silence as punishment. Bringing up old arguments to win the current one. Refusing to listen or dismissing your partner's feelings.

content.ha:
Dangantaka mai kyau tana bukatar sadarwa mai gaskiya, mai girmamawa — musamman a lokacin rikici.

Alamomin sadarwa mai kyau: Sauraron don fahimta, ba kawai don amsa ba. Bayyana ji ba tare da zargi ba ("Na ji..." ba "Kai koyaushe..."). Daukar alhakin ji na kanka. Kasancewa da niyyar daukar hutu lokacin da tattaunawa ta yi zafi.

Alamomin sadarwa mara kyau: Kira, barazana, ko amfani da shiru a matsayin hukunci. Fitar da tsoffin muhawara don lashe na yanzu. Kin sauraro ko watsi da ji na abokin tarayya.
content.yo:
Ìbáṣepọ̀ tó dára nilo ìbáṣepọ̀ tó jẹ́ òtítọ́, tó ní ìbáṣepọ̀ — pàápàá jùlọ nígbà ìja.

Àmì ìbáṣepọ̀ tó dára: Fífi ẹ̀sùn kó láti mọ, kì í ṣe láti dáhùn. Ṣíṣe àfihàn ìmọ̀lára láì fi ẹ̀sùn kàn ("Mo ní ìmọ̀lára..." kì í ṣe "Iwọ máa..."). Gbigba ẹ̀sùn fún ìmọ̀lára rẹ. Jẹ́ kí o ní ìfẹ́ láti gba ìsinmi nígbà tí ìjíròrò bá gbóná.

Àmì ìbáṣepọ̀ tó kù: Kíkọ́, ìbànújẹ, tàbí lílo ìdákẹ́jẹ gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìyà. Fífi ìjíròrò àtijọ́ sílẹ̀ láti ṣẹ́gun ìjíròrò lọwọlọwọ. Kíkọ́ láti tẹ́tí sí tàbí kó ìmọ̀lára ẹlẹ́gbẹ́ rẹ.
content.ig:
Mmekọrịta dị mma chọrọ nkwurịta okwu ziri ezi, nke na-asọpụrụ — karịsịa n'oge esemokwu.

Ihe ngosi nke nkwurịta okwu dị mma: Ịge ntị iji ghọta, ọ bụghị naanị iji zaghachi. Ikpughe mmetụta na-enweghị ịkpa oke ("Anụrụ m..." ọ bụghị "Ị na-eme..."). Iwere ọrụ maka mmetụta gị. Ịbụ onye chọrọ ịkwụsị mgbe mkparịta ụka na-ekpo ọkụ.

Ihe ngosi nke nkwurịta okwu na-adịghị mma: Ịkpa ụda, ịkpa ụta, ma ọ bụ iji silence dị ka ntaramahụhụ. Iweghachite esemokwu ochie iji merie nke ugbu a. Ịjụ ịge ntị ma ọ bụ ịhapụ mmetụta nke onye mmekọ gị.

content.en:
Emotional intelligence (EQ) is the ability to understand, express, and manage your own emotions — and to recognise the emotions of others.

Men are often taught to suppress emotions. This creates emotional illiteracy — the inability to name, process, or communicate feelings. And it damages relationships.

Building your EQ: Naming your emotions accurately. Pausing before reacting in anger. Recognising when someone you love is struggling. Being able to apologise genuinely. Asking for help when you need it.

Emotional intelligence is not weakness. It is the foundation of every strong relationship and every great leader.

content.ha:
Hankalin jiki (EQ) shine ikon fahimta, bayyana, da sarrafa ji na kanka — da kuma gane ji na wasu.

Maza yawanci ana koya musu su rufe ji. Wannan yana haifar da rashin ilimin ji — rashin ikon suna, sarrafa, ko sadar da ji. Kuma yana lalata dangantaka.

Gina EQ dinka: Sanya sunan ji dinka daidai. Tsayawa kafin ka yi fushi. Gane lokacin da wanda kake son sa yana cikin wahala. Kasancewa da ikon yin hakuri da gaske. Neman taimako lokacin da kake bukata.

Hankalin jiki ba rauni bane. Shi ne tushen kowace dangantaka mai karfi da kowanne babban shugaba.
content.yo:
Ìmọ̀ ẹ̀mí (EQ) ni agbára láti mọ, fi hàn, àti ṣakoso ìmọ̀lára rẹ — àti láti mọ ìmọ̀lára àwọn mìíràn.

Àwọn ọkùnrin máa ń kọ́ láti pa ìmọ̀lára mọ́. Èyí ń fa ìkànsí ìmọ̀lára — àìní agbára láti sọ, ṣakoso, tàbí fi hàn ìmọ̀lára. Ó sì ń bà á jẹ́ ìbáṣepọ̀.

Gbigba EQ rẹ: Sọ ìmọ̀lára rẹ ní kedere. Duro ṣáájú kí o dáhùn ní ìbànújẹ. Mọ̀ pé ẹni tí o nífẹ̀ẹ́ nínú rẹ ń jìyà. Jẹ́ kí o lè bínú gidi. Béèrè fún ìrànlọ́wọ́ nígbà tí o bá nílò rẹ.

Ìmọ̀ ẹ̀mí kì í ṣe àìlera. Ó jẹ́ ìpìlẹ̀ gbogbo ìbáṣepọ̀ tó lágbára àti gbogbo olórí tó dára.
content.ig:
Amamihe mmetụta (EQ) bụ ikike ịghọta, ikwu, na ijikwa mmetụta gị — na ịmata mmetụta nke ndị ọzọ.

A na-amụta ụmụ nwoke ka ha na-emegide mmetụta. Nke a na-emepụta amaghị ihe mmetụta — enweghị ike ịkpọ aha, ịrụ ọrụ, ma ọ bụ ikwu mmetụta. Na ọ na-emebi mmekọrịta.

Iwu EQ gị: Ịkpọ aha mmetụta gị nke ọma. Ịkwụsị tupu ịza ajụjụ n'ịhụnanya. Ịmata mgbe onye ị hụrụ n'anya na-enwe nsogbu. Ịbụ onye nwere ike ịrịọ mgbaghara n'eziokwu. Ịjụ maka enyemaka mgbe ịchọrọ ya.

Amamihe mmetụta abụghị adịghị ike. Ọ bụ isi nke mmekọrịta niile siri ike na onye ndu niile dị ukwuu.

opening_story.en:
Meet Bello.

Bello is 22, from Kano. He is walking home with his friend Danladi when Danladi grabs his girlfriend's wrist — hard — and says: "You will not embarrass me in front of my friend."

The girlfriend winces. She goes silent. She looks at the ground.

Bello sees everything. His heart pounds. He thinks: "This is not my business. They will settle it."

But then he looks at her face. He has seen that face before — on his mother, years ago.

Bello stops walking. He clears his throat. And he says: "Danladi, bros — let's go get some water. Leave her small."

It was a small moment. But it changed everything for that woman — and for Bello.

Today, we learn how to be Bello.

opening_story.ha:
Gane Bello.

Bello yana shekara 22, daga Kano. Yana tafiya gida tare da abokinsa Danladi lokacin da Danladi ya rike hannun budurwarsa — da karfi — ya ce: "Ba za ka yi mini kunya a gaban abokina ba."

Budurwar ta yi murmushi. Ta yi shiru. Ta duba kasa.

Bello ya ga komai. Zuciyarsa na bugawa. Ya yi tunani: "Wannan ba harkata ba ne. Za su warware shi."

Amma daga bisani ya kalli fuskarta. Ya taba ganin wannan fuskar a baya — a kan mahaifiyarsa, shekaru da suka wuce.

Bello ya tsaya tafiya. Ya share hancin sa. Ya ce: "Danladi, aboki — mu tafi mu samo ruwa. Ka bar ta kadan."

Wannan wani karamin lokaci ne. Amma ya canza komai ga wannan mace — da Bello.

A yau, za mu koyi yadda za mu zama Bello.
opening_story.yo:
Pẹ̀lú Bello.

Bello jẹ́ ọmọ ọdún 22, láti Kano. Ó ń rìn lọ sí ilé pẹ̀lú ọ̀rẹ́ rẹ̀ Danladi nígbà tí Danladi fi ọwọ́ rẹ̀ mú ọwọ́ ọrẹ́bìnrin rẹ — pẹ̀lú agbára — ó sì sọ pé: "Iwọ kì yóò ṣe ìkànsí fún mi ní iwájú ọ̀rẹ́ mi."

Ọrẹ́bìnrin náà yá. Ó dára. Ó ń wo ilẹ̀.

Bello rí gbogbo nkan. Ọkàn rẹ̀ ń bọ́. Ó rò pé: "Eyi kì í ṣe ìṣòro mi. Wọ́n yóò dá a sílẹ̀."

Ṣùgbọ́n nígbà tí ó wo oju rẹ, ó ti rí oju yẹn rí bẹ́ẹ̀ — lórí ìyá rẹ, ọdún mẹ́ta sẹ́yìn.

Bello dá a dúró. Ó sọ́ ẹnu rẹ. Ó sì sọ pé: "Danladi, ọ̀rẹ́ — jẹ́ ká lọ ra omi. Fọwọ́ rẹ̀ sílẹ̀ díẹ̀."

Ó jẹ́ ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ kékeré. Ṣùgbọ́n ó yí gbogbo nkan padà fún obìnrin yẹn — àti fún Bello.

Lónìí, a máa kọ́ bí a ṣe lè jẹ́ Bello.
opening_story.ig:
Nabata Bello.

Bello bụ afọ 22, si Kano. Ọ na-eje ije n'ụlọ na enyi ya Danladi mgbe Danladi jidere aka enyi nwanyị ya — nke ukwuu — na-ekwu: "I gaghị eme m ihe ọjọọ n'ihu enyi m."

Enyi nwanyị ahụ na-ama jijiji. Ọ na-ezobe. Ọ na-ele ala.

Bello hụrụ ihe niile. Obi ya na-ama jijiji. Ọ na-eche: "Nke a abụghị ọrụ m. Ha ga-edozi ya."

Ma mgbe ọ na-ele ihu ya, ọ hụrụ ihu ahụ tupu — na nne ya, afọ gara aga.

Bello kwụsịrị ije. Ọ na-ehichapụ ọnụ ya. Ọ na-ekwu: "Danladi, enyi — ka anyị gaa nweta mmiri. Hapụrụ ya obere."

Ọ bụ oge nta. Ma ọ gbanwere ihe niile maka nwanyị ahụ — na maka Bello.

Taa, anyị ga-amụta otu esi bụrụ Bello.

content.en:
Abuse is not always obvious. It does not always look like a black eye or a hospital visit.

Warning signs of abuse in relationships: A partner is controlled — their phone, money, movements, friendships. They are frequently belittled or humiliated in public. They seem afraid of their partner's reactions. They make excuses for their partner's behaviour. They are isolated from family and friends.

You do not need to be certain to be concerned. If something feels wrong, it usually is.
content.pcm:
Abuse no dey always obvious. E no dey always look like black eye or hospital visit.

Warning signs of abuse for relationship: One partner dey control — their phone, money, movements, friendships. Dem dey belittle or humiliate am for public. Dem dey fear their partner reactions. Dem dey make excuse for their partner behaviour. Dem dey isolated from family and friends.

You no need to dey sure to dey concerned. If something dey feel wrong, e usually be so.
content.ha:
Cin zarafi ba koyaushe yana bayyana ba. Ba koyaushe yana kama da ido baki ko ziyartar asibiti ba.

Alamomin gargadi na cin zarafi a cikin dangantaka: Abokin tarayya yana cikin iko — wayar su, kudi, motsi, abokai. Ana yawan raina su ko kuma a yi musu kunya a bainar jama'a. Sun yi tsoro game da martanin abokin tarayya. Sun yi uzuri ga halayen abokin tarayya. Sun rabu da iyali da abokai.

Ba lallai ne ka tabbatar don ka damu ba. Idan wani abu yana jin ba daidai ba, yawanci haka ne.
content.yo:
Ẹ̀sùn kì í ṣe pé ó dájú. Kì í ṣe pé ó máa dájú bí ẹ̀yà dudu tàbí ìbẹ̀wẹ̀ àìlera.

Àlàyé àkíyèsí ẹ̀sùn nínú ìbáṣepọ̀: Ọ̀rẹ́ kan ni a ń ṣàkóso — fónu wọn, owó, ìrìnàjò, ìbáṣepọ̀. Wọ́n máa ń kó wọn sílẹ̀ tàbí kó wọn ní ìkànsí ní àwùjọ. Wọ́n ń bẹ̀rù ìbáṣepọ̀ wọn. Wọ́n máa ń ṣe àfihàn fún ìhùwàsí ọ̀rẹ́ wọn. Wọ́n ti yà wọn kúrò ní ìdílé àti ọ̀rẹ́.

O kò ní láti jẹ́ pé o dájú láti ní ìbànújẹ. Bí nkan bá ń jẹ́ pé kò dájú, ó sábà máa jẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
content.ig:
Ime ihe ọjọọ adịghị mgbe a na-ahụ ya. Ọ bụghị mgbe niile ka ọ na-adị ka anya ojii ma ọ bụ njem n'ụlọ ọgwụ.

Ihe ngosi nke ime ihe ọjọọ na mmekọrịta: Enyi na-ahụ maka — ekwentị ha, ego, njem, enyi. A na-emekarị ka ha bụrụ ndị na-adịghị mma ma ọ bụ na-eme ka ha nwee ihere n'ịha. Ha na-atụ egwu nzaghachi enyi ha. Ha na-eme ihe mgbaghara maka omume enyi ha. Ha na-anọpụ iche na ezinụlọ na ndị enyi.

Ị chọghị ka ị bụrụ onye ziri ezi ka ị nwee nchegbu. Ọ bụrụ na ihe na-adị ka ọ na-adịghị mma, ọ na-adịkarị otú ahụ.

title.ha: Yadda Ake Tsoma Baki Cikin Harkokin Lafiya — The 5Ds
title.yo: Bí a ṣe lè Tẹ̀síwájú Lára — The 5Ds
title.ig: Otu esi Tinye aka n'Ọnọdụ Nchedo — The 5Ds

content.en:
Intervening does not mean becoming a hero or risking violence. It means doing something — however small — that disrupts the abuse.

The 5Ds of Bystander Intervention: Direct — speak up calmly ("Hey, that's not okay"). Distract — interrupt the situation ("Come, let's go"). Delegate — get someone else involved if you can't act safely. Delay — check in with the person after ("Are you okay?"). Document — record safely if it is safe to do so.

Safety first — always. If direct intervention feels dangerous, use distraction or delegation instead.
content.pcm:
Intervening no mean say you go become hero or risk violence. E mean say you go do something — no matter how small — wey go disrupt the abuse.

The 5Ds of Bystander Intervention: Direct — speak up calmly ("Hey, that one no dey okay"). Distract — interrupt the situation ("Come, make we go"). Delegate — get another person involved if you no fit act safely. Delay — check in with the person after ("Are you okay?"). Document — record safely if e dey safe to do so.

Safety first — always. If direct intervention dey feel dangerous, use distraction or delegation instead.
content.ha:
Tsoma baki ba yana nufin zama jarumi ko hadarin tashin hankali ba. Yana nufin yin wani abu — ko da kadan — wanda zai katse cin zarafin.

The 5Ds na Tsoma Baki: Kai tsaye — yi magana cikin nutsuwa ("Hey, wannan ba daidai ba ne"). Kawo hankalin — katse yanayin ("Ku zo, mu tafi"). Ba da umarni — sami wani da zai shiga idan ba za ka iya aiki lafiya ba. Jinkirta — duba tare da mutumin bayan ("Shin lafiya?"). Rubuta — rubuta lafiya idan yana da lafiya a yi haka.

Lafiya na farko — koyaushe. Idan tsoma baki kai tsaye yana jin hadari, yi amfani da jinkirta ko ba da umarni maimakon haka.
content.yo:
Tẹ̀síwájú kì í ṣe pé o di akíkanjú tàbí kó ìfarapa. Ó túmọ̀ sí pé o ṣe nkan — bí ó ti kéré tó — tí yóò dá ẹ̀sùn dúró.

The 5Ds ti Tẹ̀síwájú: Taara — sọ̀rọ̀ ní ìfarapa ("Hey, eyi kì í ṣe dáadáa"). Yà — dá ìṣòro dúró ("Ẹ jẹ́ ká lọ"). Fún ẹlòmíì — gba ẹlòmíì láti kópa bí o kò bá lè ṣiṣẹ́ ní ààbò. Dákẹ́ — ṣàyẹwo pẹ̀lú ẹni náà lẹ́yìn ("Ṣé o wà dáadáa?"). Kọ́wé — kọ́wé ní ààbò bí ó bá jẹ́ pé ó dájú láti ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀.

Ààbò ni àkọ́kọ́ — nígbà gbogbo. Bí tẹ̀síwájú taara bá ń jẹ́ pé ó ní ìfarapa, lo yà tàbí fún ẹlòmíì dipo.
content.ig:
Tinye aka apụtaghị na ị ga-abụ onye dike ma ọ bụ na ị ga-ewe iwe. Ọ pụtara na ị ga-eme ihe — n'agbanyeghị na ọ bụ obere — nke ga-egbochi ime ihe ọjọọ.

The 5Ds nke Tinye aka: N'ụzọ doro anya — kwuo nwayọọ ("Hey, nke a adịghị mma"). Dọrọ uche — kwụsị ọnọdụ ahụ ("Bịa, ka anyị gaa"). Nye onye ọzọ ọrụ — kpọọ onye ọzọ ka o sonyere ma ọ bụrụ na ị nweghị ike ime ihe n'ụzọ dị mma. Kpọchie — lelee onye ahụ mgbe e mesịrị ("Ị dị mma?"). Dezie — dezie n'ụzọ dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ọ dị mma ime ya.

Nchedo bụ isi — mgbe niile. Ọ bụrụ na itinye aka n'ụzọ doro anya na-eme ka ị nwee nchegbu, jiri dọrọ uche ma ọ bụ nye onye ọzọ ọrụ kama.

title.yo: Ìtìlẹ́yìn fún Àwọn Tí Wọ́n Ti Jà
title.ig: Nkwado maka Ndị Nwetara Ihe Ọjọọ

content.en:
If someone tells you they are being abused, your response in that moment matters enormously.

What to do: Believe them. Listen without judgment. Tell them it is not their fault. Ask what they need ("How can I support you?"). Share resources — helplines, shelters, legal support. Respect their choices — do not force them to leave if they are not ready. Check in with them regularly.

What NOT to do: Ask "What did you do to provoke it?" Advise them to "just leave" without a plan. Tell other people their story without permission. Minimise what happened.
content.pcm:
If person tell you say dem dey abuse am, your response for that moment dey very important.

Wet we go do: Believe dem. Listen without judgment. Tell dem say e no be their fault. Ask wetin dem need ("How I fit support you?"). Share resources — helplines, shelters, legal support. Respect their choices — no force dem to leave if dem no ready. Check in with dem regularly.

Wetin NO to do: Ask "Wet you do to provoke am?" Advise dem to "just leave" without plan. Tell other people their story without permission. Minimise wetin happen.
content.ha:
Idan wani ya gaya maka suna cin zarafi, martaninka a wannan lokacin yana da matukar muhimmanci.

Abin da za a yi: Ka yarda da su. Ka saurari su ba tare da hukunci ba. Ka gaya musu cewa ba laifinsu ba ne. Ka tambaye su abin da suke bukata ("Ta yaya zan iya tallafa maka?"). Raba hanyoyin taimako — layukan taimako, wuraren tsaro, tallafin shari'a. Ka girmama zabin su — kada ka tilasta musu su tafi idan ba su shirya ba. Ka duba su akai-akai.

Abin da BA za a yi ba: Tambayi "Me ka yi don ka jawo hakan?" Shawartar su da "ku tafi kawai" ba tare da shiri ba. Ka gaya wa wasu labarinsu ba tare da izini ba. Ka rage abin da ya faru.
content.yo:
Bí ẹnikan bá sọ fún ọ pé wọ́n ń ṣe ẹ̀sùn, ìbáṣepọ̀ rẹ ní àkókò yẹn jẹ́ pataki gan-an.

Kí ni a ṣe: Gba wọn. Gbọ́ láì ṣe ìdáhùn. Sọ fún wọn pé kì í ṣe ẹ̀sùn wọn. Béèrè ohun tí wọ́n nílò ("Báwo ni mo ṣe lè ràn ọ́ lọ́wọ́?"). Pín àwọn orísun — àwọn ilé ìtùnú, àwọn ilé ìtìlẹ́yìn, ìtìlẹ́yìn òfin. Bọwọ́ fún àwọn yiyan wọn — má ṣe fi wọn sílẹ̀ bí wọ́n kò bá ti ṣetan. Ṣàyẹwo wọn nígbà gbogbo.

Kí ni KÒ láti ṣe: Béèrè "Kí ni o ṣe láti fa a?" Fún wọn ní ìmúra láti "kó lọ" láì ní ètò. Sọ ìtàn wọn fún àwọn míì láì ní ìmúra. Kó ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà kéré.
content.ig:
Ọ bụrụ na onye na-agwa gị na ha na-eme ihe ọjọọ, nzaghachi gị n'oge ahụ dị oke mkpa.

Ihe ị ga-eme: Kweta ha. Gee ntị na-enweghị ikpe. Gwa ha na ọ bụghị mmejọ ha. Jụọ ihe ha chọrọ ("Kedu ka m ga-esi nyere gị? "). Kekọrịta ihe ndị a — nọmba enyemaka, ụlọ nkwado, nkwado iwu. Kwere nhọrọ ha — egbula ha iwepụ ma ọ bụrụ na ha adịghị njikere. Lelee ha mgbe niile.

Ihe KỌMỌ ga-eme: Jụọ "Kedu ihe ị mere iji kpalite ya?" Nye ha ndụmọdụ ka "hapụ ya" na-enweghị atụmatụ. Gwa ndị ọzọ akụkọ ha na-enweghị ikike. Kwepụ ihe mere.

feedback.en: Correct. Fear of a partner's reactions — walking on eggshells, flinching, excessive appeasement — is one of the clearest warning signs of an abusive relationship.

feedback.ig: Ziri ezi. Ịtụ egwu nzaghachi enyi — na-anya n'elu akwa, na-atụ egwu, na-eme ihe na-adịghị mma — bụ otu n'ime ihe ngosi doro anya nke mmekọrịta ime ihe ọjọọ.

opening_story.en:
Meet Tonye.

Tonye is 21, from Yenagoa. He is the most respected person in his friend group. When he speaks, everyone listens.

One night, the boys are drinking and one of them starts talking about a girl in degrading terms. Everyone laughs. The conversation escalates.

Tonye laughs too — at first.

But then he thinks of his 16-year-old sister. And he imagines someone talking about her this way.

He stops laughing. He says: "Abeg, that's somebody's sister. Let's change the topic."

There is a moment of silence. And then someone else says: "You're right. My bad." The conversation shifts.

Tonye didn't give a speech. He didn't shout. He just used the influence he already had — and it worked.
opening_story.pcm:
